reviews.title: Greatest card for performance and price
reviews.comment:
I’ve been using the RX 9060 XT 16GB and overall it’s been a great experience for what it is. Performance is solid across modern games — most titles run smoothly at 1080p and even 1440p without constantly needing to turn down settings. The 16GB of VRAM really helps in games that like a lot of textures or higher frame buffers, so you feel a bit more future-proofed than with lower-VRAM cards.
Thermals and noise have been good too. It doesn’t run insanely hot, and the fans stay fairly quiet unless you’re really pushing it. Even under heavy load the noise level stays reasonable, so it doesn’t feel like a jet engine in your case.
I’ve also noticed that it handles creative workloads pretty well. Video editing and 3D work feel snappier than what I was used to before, and exporting/rendering seems a bit quicker thanks to the extra memory and compute headroom.
It’s not the absolute fastest card on the market, but it’s definitely a strong mid-to-upper-mid performer for its price point. If you want a GPU that can handle current games at good quality settings and won’t get in its own way thermally or acoustically, the RX 9060 XT 16GB is an easy card to recommend.
reviews.author: Mehran

reviews.title: The ASUS RX 9060 XT 16GB is Awesome!
reviews.comment:
Seriously, the ASUS Dual Radeon RX 9060 XT is the champ when it comes to budget 1440p gaming right now. I snagged mine on Black Friday, and the value is just unbelievable for the price I paid. You really can't find anything better for the money.
ASUS is definitely my go-to manufacturer for AMD cards. They've got the best quality designs, solid components, and their customer service is great. This card is totally up to that standard.
This thing absolutely crushes 1440p gaming. What really makes it 'future proof' is the huge 16GB of VRAM! That's more than enough for gaming, plus it handles home AI/ML models well with ROCm. Best part? It's super quiet even when it's really working hard. OK, it's 2.5 slots thick, but it's actually pretty short, so it fits nicely into smaller PC cases, which is handy for your build flexibility. All those YouTube reviews saying this is the best value? They're totally right. It's just an awesome card, highly recommend!
reviews.author: Denis F.

reviews.title: very pleased, no issues, performs well
reviews.comment:
I have had the card since late December 2025. I chose this card because I wanted the option of VR, and my previous card did not officially support that (Arc). Also it was an upgrade to 16GB of VRAM for me. I didn't have any issues installing it, it was literally minutes to swap the cards and start installing drivers.
I did have a little difficulty finding/changing some settings in the drivers, but that may be my fault. I had zero issues installing the drivers, and have no conflicts, even though I also have Intel drivers installed for the iGPU (encoding).
I have this paired with an Intel i5-12600k (mildly overclocked) on an Asrock Z790 PG Lightning D4 motherboard with 32GB (2x16) of RAM (I do not remember the exact ram specifications, but it is not a high-performance kit). Graphics appear smooth at 1440p.
I am not really a gamer, but I have played Destiny 2 on this system for a good number of hours. Left completely to its own devices, the system can approach a maximum of 180fps at 1440p. I don't really need every last frame (not an amazing gamer, after all) so I set a limit of 120 and that's where it stays.
I have had zero overheating issues, even if I allow the GPU to approach 100% utilization. The fans are not noisy when running, it sits right next to me and does not interfere with a microphone at all. (I do have an AIO). I don't think I've seen it even approach max temps.
The card itself appears well built.
I chose this particular GPU because the form factor is ideal for the case (modified old PC case with limited room). This card also uses less power than my previous 8gb Arc GPU.
Side note: I also noticed the rear vents are well placed, even though my case has bars between the slot openings (not designed for multi-slot expansion cards), the vents are not blocked.
I am very pleased so far, and barring any major problems in the near future, I would definitely consider both AMD Radeon and Asus again.
